home_features_title: The whole SSH workflow, without the terminal gymnastics.
home_features_subtitle: Six tools that usually live across a dozen man pages, dotfiles, and shell aliases — rebuilt as one focused Mac app.
home_feat1_desc: Edit ~/.ssh/config visually. Reorder hosts, tweak directives, manage Includes — comments and formatting are preserved byte-for-byte.
home_feat2_desc: Run -L, -R, and -D forwards over a single SSH link. Multiple forwards per tunnel, live throughput, and auto-retry with backoff.
home_feat3_desc: Inspect and use ed25519, ECDSA, and RSA keys. ssh-agent and external-signer auth are built in — passphrase keys decrypt natively.
home_feat4_desc: Search, review, and prune known_hosts. New hosts get a TOFU prompt with full fingerprint verification before you ever connect.
home_feat5_desc: A git-style time machine for your config. Every edit is a content-addressed commit you can diff, branch, and restore in one click.
home_feat6_desc: Chain bastions with ProxyJump and SSH Config Manager builds the entire path in-process — no nested ssh subprocess, no shell required.
home_lossless1: Comments, blank lines, and indentation survive every save
home_lossless2: Include directives are parsed and followed, never flattened
home_lossless3: App-only data (tunnels, tags, favorites) never touches your config
home_config_desc: A lossless parser reads and rewrites your config so the bytes you didn’t touch stay exactly as they were. Hand-edit in a real editor, or let the UI do it.
home_tunnels_title: Tunnels that run inside the app.
home_tunnels_desc: Because the sandbox can’t cleanly launch Terminal, SSH Config Manager speaks SSH itself — over swift-nio-ssh. Start a tunnel and it’s supervised: health-checked, retried with backoff, and metered live.
home_security_title: Built for the sandbox, not around it.
home_security_subtitle: SSH Config Manager treats your keys and network access as privileges, not assumptions. The architecture is the security story.
home_sec1_desc: Full com.apple.security.app-sandbox entitlement. ~/.ssh access is a user-granted, security-scoped bookmark — nothing else is touched.
home_sec2_desc: The engine speaks SSH in-process over swift-nio-ssh. No ssh subprocess, no Terminal, no quarantine stripping.
home_sec3_desc: Private keys and passphrases are protected by the system Keychain and verified against known_hosts on every connect.
roadmap_seo_title: Roadmap — SSH Config Manager for macOS and Linux
roadmap_seo_description: What comes next for SSH Config Manager: tunnel domains, import from other tools, cloud provider import, and more.
roadmap_hero_title: Where SSH Config Manager is headed.
roadmap_hero_subtitle: A look at what's building now and what's coming. These are directions, not dated promises — the order shifts with what you tell us matters most.
roadmap_col_later_hint: On the table, not yet scheduled
roadmap_now1_title: Open in VS Code Remote / Cursor
roadmap_now1_text: Launch any host straight into a remote editing session with one click.
roadmap_next1_text: Reach a -L forward by name — https://app.tnl, no port, no /etc/hosts — via NetworkExtension.
roadmap_next2_text: Pull sessions from Termius, PuTTY (.ppk), or another machine's config.
roadmap_next3_text: Opt-in TCP pings light up green/red status dots next to every host.
roadmap_next4_text: Timestamped backups of the whole ~/.ssh, and a 3-way diff when files change underneath you.
roadmap_later1_text: Generate hosts from your AWS, GCP, Hetzner, or DigitalOcean instances.
roadmap_later2_text: Detect and prefer these SSH agents when they're present.
roadmap_later3_text: Open any host from Raycast or from a link.
roadmap_later4_text: A structured editor for Match conditions, and directive changes across many hosts at once.
roadmap_shipped1_text: A GTK4 and libadwaita app on the same Swift core, with .deb, .rpm and Flatpak packages.
roadmap_shipped2_text: Back up your config to a private gist, with optional end-to-end encryption and a conflict prompt.
roadmap_shipped3_text: Sort hosts into collapsible groups in the sidebar.
roadmap_shipped4_text: Find any host in Spotlight and open it in the app.
roadmap_shipped5_text: Flag weak algorithms, passphrase-less keys, world-readable files, and orphaned keys.
roadmap_shipped6_text: -L/-R/-D forwards with multi-hop ProxyJump, fully supervised.
roadmap_shipped7_text: Diff, branch, and restore any config version.
roadmap_shipped8_text: Push a public key to a host's authorized_keys.
roadmap_shipped9_text: View loaded identities; add, remove, and persist them.
roadmap_shipped_subtitle: The roadmap is real — here's a slice of what already moved from "next" to "done".
roadmap_cta_subtitle: The roadmap is shaped by the people who use the app. Tell us what would make your SSH workflow better.
home_seo_title_oss: SSH Config Manager — open-source SSH configs, keys and tunnels
home_seo_description_oss: A free, open-source native app for macOS and Linux. Edit ~/.ssh/config losslessly, manage keys and known_hosts, and run in-process SSH tunnels. Every feature is free.
home_hero_subtitle_oss: Manage every host, key, tunnel and agent from one native app. Free, open source, and complete — there is no paid tier.
home_support_title: The app is free. Support is optional.
home_support_desc: SSH Config Manager costs nothing and locks nothing. If it saves you time, there are three ways to give something back.
home_support_appstore_title: Buy it on the Mac App Store — {price}
home_support_appstore_desc: The same app, with automatic updates and Apple signing handled for you. The {price} goes straight into development.
home_support_sponsor_desc: A one-time or monthly sponsorship funds the work directly, with no store cut.
home_support_contribute_desc: Report a bug, review a pull request, or ship a feature you want. The whole app is on GitHub.
home_support_note: Every feature is free in every build. There is no paid tier.
home_cta_desc_oss: Download a build from GitHub Releases, or install from the Mac App Store to support the work.
footer_tagline_oss: The open-source way to manage SSH configs, keys, known_hosts and in-process tunnels.
home_download_title: Install SSH Config Manager on macOS or Linux.
home_download_desc: Every build has every feature. Pick the package that fits your system.
home_download_macos_desc: Needs macOS 15 or later. Install from the Mac App Store, or download the build from GitHub Releases.
home_download_linux_desc: A native GTK4 and libadwaita app. The packages need libadwaita 1.6 or later. The Flatpak bundle brings its own runtime.
home_download_linux_note: All Linux files are on the latest GitHub release.
privacy_seo_description: SSH Config Manager collects no data. The app has no telemetry, and the website has no analytics, cookies or forms.
privacy_hero_subtitle: SSH Config Manager collects no data about you. This page tells you where your data goes when you use the app and this website.
privacy_hl1_body: The app has no account, no analytics and no telemetry. Your configs, keys and tunnels stay on your computer.
privacy_hl2_body: Gist sync uses your own GitHub token. You can encrypt the data before it leaves your computer.
privacy_hl3_body: The website has no analytics, no cookies and no forms.
privacy_overview_p1: SSH Config Manager is an open-source app for macOS and Linux. It edits your SSH configuration, manages keys and known_hosts, and runs SSH tunnels. The app and this website collect no personal data. This policy applies to the app, to Gist sync and to this website.
privacy_app_intro: The app runs on your computer and needs no account. In detail:
privacy_app_item1: No analytics, no telemetry and no crash reports
privacy_app_item2: No advertising and no advertising code
privacy_app_item3: No upload of your SSH configuration, keys or known_hosts to a server that you did not choose
privacy_app_outro: The app keeps its data on your computer. On macOS, passphrases and tokens stay in the macOS Keychain. The app connects only to the hosts that you connect to and, when you turn on Gist sync, to GitHub.
privacy_sync_p1: Gist sync is optional. When you turn it on, the app sends your synced data only to GitHub. The app uses your own GitHub token and keeps it in the macOS Keychain.
privacy_sync_p2: You can encrypt the data with a passphrase before the app sends it. GitHub then keeps only the encrypted data. GitHub processes this data under the GitHub Privacy Statement.
privacy_website_p1: This website is a set of static files. It has no analytics, no cookies, no forms and no third-party scripts.
privacy_website_p2: GitHub Pages hosts this website. GitHub keeps standard access logs, for example IP addresses and request times, to operate and protect the service. The project does not get these logs.
privacy_changes_p1: This policy can change. When it changes, the “Last updated” date at the top of this page changes too.
